raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

`ReplayBuffer._wait_for_next_poll()` sleeps a hard-coded `poll_interval=2.0` between TransferQueue metadata syncs (used
by both the sync `sample()` and the async `wait_for_sampleable()`). The trainer therefore notices the last finished
prompt up to 2 s late, and `timing_s/gen` is quantized to multiples of 2 s (main, vLLM: 2.21, 4.21, 4.21, 2.21 … s;
SGLang: 2.28 s every step). This PR replaces the sleep with a wait on a small completion counter that rollout workers
bump when a prompt reaches a terminal status. On 8x MI355X GSM8K GRPO it cuts `timing_s/gen` by 22–31% and step time by
~10%, with no extra TransferQueue metadata traffic.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+replay_buffer+poll_interval
  No open or closed PR wakes the sampler on rollout completion. Related: #8203 (draft) replaces `replay_buffer.py` with
  `StreamingDataloaderAsync`, whose coordinator wakes on sample requests and refills but still finds finished prompts
  only on the next `poll_interval`. If #8203 lands first I'm happy to port this onto it: the completion notification
  would just set its `_wakeup` event (with the same `need` threshold to keep metadata syncs low).
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

Unit (CPU):
```bash
pytest -q tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_replay_buffer_on_cpu.py \
          tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_v1_async_alignment_on_cpu.py \
          tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_separate_async_step_switch_on_cpu.py
```
main (4b26c78): 130 passed; with this PR: 132 passed (2 new: `test_sample_wakes_on_completion_notification[sync|async]`,
`poll_interval=30`, a prompt goes `running → finished` + notify, `sample()` must return within 5 s).

End-to-end A/B (main 4b26c78 vs main + this PR): 8x MI355X (ROCm 7.14), Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, GSM8K GRPO, batch 128 x
n=4, 15 steps, colocated FSDP, sync trainer. Both arms on the same node in one job, interleaved (main, PR, main, PR)
per rollout engine; mean over 2 runs of the per-run mean of steps 3–15.

| | vLLM main → PR | SGLang main → PR |
|---|---|---|
| `timing_s/gen` | 2.78 → 1.92 s (−31%) | 2.43 → 1.90 s (−22%) |
| `timing_s/step` | 7.29 → 6.50 s (−10.8%) | 7.39 → 6.69 s (−9.5%) |
| `perf/throughput` | +12.3% | +9.4% |
| `kv_list` metadata syncs per `sample()` | 2.27 → 2.30 | 2.07 → 2.20 |
| final GSM8K val acc (mean of 2 runs) | 0.404 → 0.422 | 0.432 → 0.415 (run-to-run noise) |

With this PR `timing_s/gen` is no longer quantized (1.65–2.49 s). Notify-to-wake latency is ~1.4 ms. The gain is
largest for short steps (small models, short rollouts, async / frequent weight sync); for 40 s+ steps it is ≤ ~2 s/step.

### API and Usage Example

No user-facing API or config change. `poll_interval` keeps its meaning as the maximum wait between syncs (now a
fallback timeout). Internally `_wait_for_next_poll()` gains an optional `need: int = 1` argument, so existing
subclasses that call or override it keep working.

### Design & Code Changes

- `CompletionNotifier` (async Ray actor, `num_cpus=0`): per-partition counter + `asyncio.Condition`.
- `completion_notifier()`: process-wide handle to the named actor (`get_if_exists=True`), cached per Ray job id and
  shared by producers and the replay buffer, so it outlives individual `ReplayBuffer` instances.
- `AgentLoopWorkerTQ._run_prompt`: after publishing the terminal status (`finished` / `failure`), call
  `notify(partition_id)` (best effort).
- `_wait_for_next_poll(..., need)`: wait until the counter grows by `need` — prompts still missing, or the in-flight
  count while DAPO drains — or until `poll_interval`. The counter kept from the previous wake is read before the
  caller's next metadata sync and producers notify only after the status write is acknowledged, so a wake can be early
  (one extra sync) but never late. Waiting for `need` instead of every completion keeps metadata syncs at ~2 per
  `sample()` (waking on every completion gave the same speedup but 43–65 syncs).
- If the notifier is unavailable (no Ray, actor died) the wait falls back to `time.sleep(poll_interval)`, i.e. the
  current behavior.

Diff: 3 files, +95/−4 (including a 25-line test).

AI assistance was used while developing this change.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide.
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks (all hooks pass on the changed files).
- [ ] Add / Update the documentation. (Not applicable: no user-facing behavior or config change.)
- [x] Add unit test(s) covering the change (`test_replay_buffer_on_cpu.py` runs in the CPU unit-test workflow).
- [ ] Request CI in the `ci-request` Slack channel once ready.

+

+    finally:
+        _clear_partition(partition_id)

+NOTIFIER_NAME = "verl_replay_buffer_notifier"
+
+
+@ray.remote(num_cpus=0)
+class CompletionNotifier:
+    """Per-partition counter of prompts that reached a terminal status, so the replay buffer can block until enough
+    of them finished instead of polling TransferQueue every ``poll_interval`` seconds."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self._seq, self._cond = {}, asyncio.Condition()
+
+    async def notify(self, partition_id: str):
+        async with self._cond:
+            self._seq[partition_id] = self._seq.get(partition_id, 0) + 1
+            self._cond.notify_all()
+
+    async def wait(self, partition_id: str, since: int, timeout: float) -> int:
+        async with self._cond:
+            try:
+                await asyncio.wait_for(self._cond.wait_for(lambda: self._seq.get(partition_id, 0) > since), timeout)
+            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
+                pass
+            return self._seq.get(partition_id, 0)
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _notifier_for_job(job_id: str):
+    return CompletionNotifier.options(name=NOTIFIER_NAME, get_if_exists=True).remote()
+
+
+def completion_notifier():
+    """Process-wide handle to the named CompletionNotifier, shared by producers and the replay buffer.
+
+    Cached per process (not per ReplayBuffer) so the actor outlives individual ReplayBuffer instances; a new Ray job
+    id (e.g. after a Ray restart) re-creates it."""
+    return _notifier_for_job(ray.get_runtime_context().get_job_id())
+

+    def _wait_for_next_poll(self, partition_id: str, last_debug_time: float, need: int = 1) -> float:
